question.text: The difference of speed of light in the two media <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>A</mi></msub><mo>-</mo><msub><mi>v</mi><mi>B</mi></msub></mrow></mfenced></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>7</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>. If the refractive index of medium <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>47</mn></math>, then the ratio of refractive index of medium <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> to medium <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>A</mi></math> is: (Given : speed of light in vacuum <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>8</mn></msup><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
The speed of light in the medium B will be, vB=cμB

The speed of light in the medium A will be, vA=cμA.

Now, 

vA-vB=c1μA-1μB⇒2.6×107=3×108×1μA-11.47⇒μA=1.13
